notes: THE DEFECT: the startup-liveness fuse (T586) in tools/runner read STDOUT ONLY, and `pi` buffers stdout to completion, so a lane that IS reading its bundle and working writes only its session JSONL and looks silent to the fuse. T735 attempt 2 (ox-alpha, raw `pi --provider openrouter` — the invocation the operator wants kept) was killed at wall 600.9 s with the note 'startup liveness timeout 600s (10'00) — agent lane produced no output since launch (bundle never read?)'. Its session file (session ~/.pi/agent/sessions/--Users-alex-Project-Zig-weizigo--/2026-08-23T10-47-35-328Z_*.jsonl, first record +1.3 s after launch, last record 0.2 s before the kill) holds 86 records, 40 assistant turns, 19,060 output tokens. The note is worse than the kill: 'bundle never read?' is a CAUSAL CLAIM about the model that the evidence refutes — the standing killed_by / stop-never-attribute discipline. This is the third documented instance of the same blind spot (T447 qwen: 'no completion inside 40 minutes, not produced nothing'; Race F T616: winning claude-opus-5 lane killed at 600.8 s with its 43 KB deliverable written, recorded verified=fail). THE FIX (tools/runner, T773): (1) the startup fuse for a pi/ollama lane no longer reads stdout alone — the sensor set adds the pi session file's mtime: under `--session <path>` the exact file, else the cwd-slug session dir ~/.pi/agent/sessions/<cwd-slug>/ (token-capture.py's slug()/default_sessions_dir — the same fallback T751 owes the token meter; one resolution `_pi_session_scan_target` serves both consumers; WEIZIGO_PI_SESSIONS_DIR is the test hook mirroring WEIZIGO_CLAUDE_TRANSCRIPT_DIR). A lane writing its session is alive, whatever the stream says; the fuse fires only when BOTH the stream and the session sensor have been silent for the whole window (last_pi_session_activity starts at launch, so a genuinely dead lane still dies at --startup-timeout exactly as before). (2) The kill note states what was measured, never a cause: 'startup liveness timeout Ns (fmt) — no stdout bytes since launch; no pi session activity since launch (sensor: pi session file/dir '<path>')'. NO KILL NOTE IN THE FIXED RUNNER ASSERTS A CAUSE — grep of every kill_reason string: 'host memory pressure — avail X MB < floor Y MB (largest member pid N RSS M MB)' (measurement), 'liveness timeout Ns — claude lane showed no mtime movement (deliverables/session transcript) for Xs' (measurement), 'progress timeout Ns — no [progress] for Xs' (measurement), 'startup liveness timeout Ns — no stdout bytes since launch; <session reading>' (measurement, T773), 'wall ceiling Ns reached at Xs elapsed (no [progress] lines seen)' (measurement), 'CPU ceiling Ns exceeded (Xs total) (no [progress] lines seen)' (measurement), 'directive ...' (a directive, not a cause). The string 'bundle never read' exists in the file only inside two comments documenting the historical defect, never in an emitted note (grep -n shows lines 1617/3330, both comments). KILL CENSUS (item 3, the cost of the defect): every recorded kill by a stdout-class fuse of an agent lane has a session file (or, for claude T616, a 43 KB deliverable on disk) proving the lane was working — 8 of 8: T526 (pi/flash, progress-timeout 1129.6 s, session 42 turns, last record at 47% of kill wall), T573 (pi/pro, wall-ceiling 2701.0 s, session 119 turns, 50%), T616 (claude/opus, startup-liveness 600.8 s, deliverable on disk), T628 (pi/flash, progress-timeout 1463.2 s, session 66 turns, 59%), T635 (pi/pro, progress-timeout 1732.6 s, session 104 turns, 65%), T638 (pi/flash, progress-timeout 1901.3 s, session 71 turns, 68%, 25/25 verdicts complete), T643 (pi/pro, progress-timeout 1706.8 s, session 73 turns, 65%), T735 (pi/ox-alpha, startup-liveness 600.9 s, session 40 turns, 100% — the worked example). Method: matched each record's start timestamp to a session file in the cwd-slug dir within ±30 s (the two pre-T650 overwritten records, T526/T635, matched by the bundle prompt in the session head; their kills are proven by untracked/log/t526.log and t635.log '[runner] KILL: progress timeout 600s' at the _LOG_ONLY_KILLED_ATTEMPTS walls), then parsed each session: records, assistant turns, usage presence, first/last record timestamps, last-record offset as a fraction of the kill wall. All eight show assistant turns with real usage objects and the last record lands 47-100% of the way through the kill window. ZERO recorded kills in the class are provably idle. The remaining recorded agent-lane kills are host-pressure/RSS kills (T527, T531, T630, T636, T661, T696, T697, T699, T721, T724) — a different class whose notes already measure (avail/floor/RSS), not the defect's; T636's session shows work to 100% of wall, and T630/T661/T699/T721 carry session_path records. TEST-FIRST (standing rule): wrote tools/regression-runner-pi-session-liveness.sh BEFORE the fix and showed it RED against HEAD: survives-session arm -> '[runner] KILL: startup liveness timeout 2s (2s) — agent lane produced no output since launch (bundle never read?)' exit 124 while sess.jsonl was being written (the T735 shape); survives-fallback arm -> exit 124 while the session dir was growing; hung arm -> note still asserted 'bundle never read?'. GREEN after the fix (all four arms): survives-session exit 0, survives-fallback exit 0, hung exit 124 with 'no stdout bytes since launch; no pi session activity since launch (sensor: ...)' and the 'bundle never read' grep empty, scoping (non-agent sleep untouched) exit 0. Regression wired into zig build test (build.zig, after the T586 startup-liveness block). All pre-existing runner regressions stay green: startup-liveness (3 passes), claude-liveness (3), agent-progress (5), reporting, run-records, brief-telemetry, harness-p95, taskid, guard, reap, host-guard, pi-session-liveness (4). SCOPE NOTE: the progress watchdog keeps T643's deliverable-mtime sensor and its derived 3 x p95 thresholds — T773 changes only the STARTUP fuse's sensor set and note, which is the fuse that killed T735/T616. A fully-silent lane that writes its session forever but never a deliverable is bounded by the wall/CPU fallback exactly as before (a lane with zero stdout never reaches the derived progress watchdog); that is the pre-existing silent-child semantics, unchanged. Landmark: advances L1 (measurement integrity) — a fleet-reliability event stops being recorded as a model-quality event. Evidence: findings/T773-context.json (census script output, red/green quotes) — committed alongside.
